decisions.title: Legacy dashboard versus V2
decisions.context: The stable Story UI uses whole-file dashboard JSON while V2 has SQLite, coverage, claims and evidence APIs.
decisions.recommendation: Use a strangler migration: freeze the legacy Story path except maintenance; route every new System/Research lens through V2; migrate old surfaces only when touched.

options.label: Strangler migration
options.description: Protects the public experience while steadily eliminating the split data plane.

options.label: Rewrite legacy onto V2 now
options.description: Architecturally clean, but high regression risk before product learning.

options.label: Maintain both indefinitely
options.description: Lowest immediate effort but doubles semantics, testing and privacy review.

decisions.title: #174 analytical method split
decisions.context: Integration-tail analysis needs censoring and competing-outcome handling without turning Product into a numerical research runtime.
decisions.recommendation: Product computes deterministic Kaplan–Meier, cumulative-incidence/risk tables and bootstrap uncertainty; Lab owns AFT/model sensitivity and exports reviewed findings later.

options.label: Deterministic Product, model sensitivity in Lab
options.description: Matches repository roles and keeps the product inspectable.

options.label: Implement AFT in Product now
options.description: One runtime, but adds optimizer/model complexity to the trusted product path.

options.label: Use medians and bins only
options.description: Simple, but mishandles open/censored work and competing outcomes.

decisions.title: #174 cohort and support floor
decisions.context: A first version must avoid left truncation, tiny-group overclaiming and arbitrary universal thresholds.
decisions.recommendation: Use PRs created inside the explicit window; merged is the event, closed-unmerged a competing outcome, open at window end right-censored. Start with versioned provisional floors: 20 eligible, 10 merge events, 5 per group.

options.label: Created-in-window + versioned floors
options.description: Auditable and implementable now; revise after synthetic and owner-data calibration.

options.label: All PRs active in window
options.description: More data, but requires careful left-truncation machinery immediately.

options.label: Render every sample size
options.description: Avoids arbitrary cutoffs but encourages unstable visual claims.

decisions.title: Windows 8.3 path failure
decisions.context: The local full suite can fail because test temporary paths arrive in 8.3 short form while root identity checks demand the canonical long form.
decisions.recommendation: Canonicalize fixture-owned temporary roots before invoking the production boundary; retain strict production root identity until a separately reviewed security change.

options.label: Fix test fixture roots first
options.description: Restores trustworthy local testing without weakening production confinement.

options.label: Normalize inside production captureRoot
options.description: Broader convenience, but changes an identity guarantee and needs deeper hostile-path review.

decisions.title: Loopback API authorization
decisions.context: Binding only to 127.0.0.1 is a useful boundary but other same-machine browser contexts/processes may reach a predictable local port.
decisions.recommendation: Treat a per-launch bearer/CSRF-bound session token as a packaging gate for CLI/desktop, not a blocker for the current synthetic/source-run release.

options.label: Add token before packaged distribution
options.description: Right-sized timing: protect broader install contexts without derailing v0.1.

options.label: Implement before v0.1
options.description: Stronger immediately, but expands the release critical path without a demonstrated current caller.

options.label: Rely on loopback only
options.description: Simpler, but insufficient once casual desktop/browser launching broadens exposure.

decisions.title: Real-data activation order
decisions.context: The project authorizes bounded real local data in principle, but source/sink policy and readiness work remain incomplete.
decisions.recommendation: Complete #174 on invented stores, then #201, then #202, then one owner-selected public metadata canary with deletion/replay proof.

options.label: #174 → #201 → #202 → canary
options.description: Proves product value before spending more effort on activation plumbing.

options.label: Finish activation before #174
options.description: Makes real input possible sooner, but risks building ingestion without a valuable consumer.

options.label: Stay synthetic indefinitely
options.description: Safest, but prevents the standalone product from proving its real utility.

decisions.title: Cross-repository C4 content hashes
decisions.context: q-6 leaves durable content-hash linkage and deletion cascade unresolved; hashes can become stable sensitive join keys.
decisions.recommendation: Do not persist cross-repository C4 hashes by default. Use ephemeral per-analysis hashes or installation-keyed, purpose-scoped HMACs with explicit retention/deletion if the feature becomes necessary.

options.label: No durable cross-repo hash by default
options.description: Avoids creating a hidden identity graph before a concrete lens needs it.

options.label: Persist purpose-scoped keyed hashes
options.description: Enables linkage with bounded risk, but only after a named product need.

options.label: Persist raw content hashes
options.description: Convenient, but creates durable correlators and deletion complexity.
